L1.description: Complete measurements precede candidate energy aggregation
L1.stage1: NuXmv R1: COMPUTE_ENERGY implies all NTERMS groups of the evaluation are measured
L1.stage2: DejaVu L1_groupsBeforeEnergy and Python unique candidate/group completeness
assumptions: Group events identify the actual measurement executions
L1.comparison: PROVED and observed obligations satisfied yield AGREEMENT; missing raw evidence is reported explicitly
L1.non_vacuity: Stage 1: witness EF COMPUTE_ENERGY holds and the early-aggregation mutant is detected. Stage 2: Python obligation groups_before_energy fires at every evaluation; DejaVu L1 fires on every energy event, and the two counts must match

L2.description: All three candidate validations precede optimizer commitment
L2.stage1: NuXmv R4: OPTIMIZER_STEP implies NCANDS validated candidate energies; R2: a stop decision after an update follows validated energies
L2.stage2: DejaVu L2_validationsBeforeCommit and Python certification of each numericValid event
assumptions: Recorded commit events correspond to actual controller boundaries
L2.comparison: A premature observed commit is DISAGREEMENT
L2.non_vacuity: Stage 1: witnesses EF OPTIMIZER_STEP and EF (CHECK_STOP & iter > 0) hold and the skipped-candidate mutant is detected. Stage 2: Python obligations validation_certified (each numericValid) and validations_before_commit (each commit) fire; DejaVu commit and validated counts must match them

L3.description: Evaluation identity and parameter provenance remain current
L3.stage1: NuXmv R3/F1-F4: bound circuit before measurement, (iteration, candidate) version of the binding and the energy, readiness reset per evaluation and per iteration
L3.stage2: DejaVu causal links and Python run/update/candidate/index/angle identity checks
assumptions: Iteration/candidate version numbers preserve current-versus-stale meaning; concrete unique IDs are a runtime strengthening, not a NuXmv proof over arbitrary strings
L3.comparison: Compare freshness with the declared abstraction boundary
L3.non_vacuity: Stage 1: witnesses for measurement, aggregation, commitment, binding and iteration restart hold, and the no-reset, stale-readiness, skipped-rebind, stale-binding, wrong-candidate and stale-energy mutants are detected. Stage 2: Python obligations evaluation_identity_current (each measurement/evaluation/validation) and commit_identity_current (each commit) fire

L4.description: Termination is final and has the declared reason
L4.stage1: NuXmv T1-T9 and E1-E6: termination, absorbing DONE/ABORT, DONE by convergence or exhausted budget with its reason, every error aborts at once with its cause and nothing else aborts, update accounting and bound, returned energy
L4.stage2: DejaVu no activity after stop; Python terminal reason, ideal-success oracle, and update budget
assumptions: Ideal-energy success is the benchmark oracle; the logical success flag abstracts this classification
L4.comparison: Missing termination is INCONCLUSIVE; an invalid reason or later activity is DISAGREEMENT
L4.non_vacuity: Stage 1: witnesses for every terminal state, the last commitment, each termination cause and each error cause hold; the defensive default branch is unreachable; the ignored-error, budget-to-abort, success-to-abort and budget-overrun mutants are detected. Stage 2: Python obligation terminal_reason fires once per closed trace; DejaVu stopped count must match

N1.description: Raw counts normalize to the reported expectations
N1.stage1: Dafny NormalizeExpectation: positive shots and valid negative counts imply normalization and [-1,1]
N1.stage2: Independent negative-eigenvalue parity counts and exact Fraction expectations
N1.comparison: Valid-input output errors: DISAGREEMENT; invalid inputs: ASSUMPTION_MISMATCH; missing counts: INCONCLUSIVE
N1.non_vacuity: Stage 2: obligation expectation_reconstructed fires for every term of every complete evaluation (4 terms x 3 candidates per update)

N2.description: Declared coefficients and measurements produce the actual energy
N2.stage1: Dafny TermEnergyContribution, ComputeTermEnergies, AggregateEnergy and supporting lemmas
N2.stage2: Exact rational reconstruction; compare contributions, score, reported energy and actual optimizer inputs
assumptions: Frozen tolerance for mathematical real versus observed floating-point values
N2.comparison: Runtime checks actual outputs; Dafny does not prove the entire Python implementation
N2.non_vacuity: Stage 2: obligation energy_reconstructed fires for every complete candidate evaluation (3 per update)

N3.description: Unique measurement groups determine physical shot consumption
N3.stage2: Validate raw group totals and accumulate each candidate/group key once
N3.comparison: Accounting errors: DISAGREEMENT; changed allocation: ASSUMPTION_MISMATCH, invalidating P1-P3 applicability
N3.non_vacuity: Stage 2: obligations allocation_checked (each valid group measurement, 9 per update) and cumulative_total_checked (each commit and the terminal event) fire

N4.description: Candidate generation and selection preserve the parameter grid
N4.stage2: Recompute modular candidates and exact-energy argmin with declared tie priority; check bound angles
assumptions: Angle conversion and quantum gate implementation are in the trusted base
N4.comparison: Compare observed indices, angles, selection and successor with the finite-grid transition
N4.non_vacuity: Stage 2: obligations candidates_generated (each update start) and selection_checked (each commit) fire

P1.description: Probability of first success within the update bound
P1.stage1: Storm bounded reachability in the Gaussian DTMC at frozen checkpoints
P1.stage2: First-success proportions from repeated independent finite-shot executions
assumptions: Same circuit, optimizer, grouping, shots, stopping predicate and update unit
Declared Gaussian approximation and numerical integration
P1.comparison: Model probability inside runtime 95% Wilson interval means AGREEMENT; final bound is primary; no joint-coverage or distributional-equivalence claim

P2.description: Expected first-success update conditional on bounded success
P2.stage1: Python propagation of the Gaussian kernel, with checkpoint CDF independently checked by Storm
P2.stage2: Mean first-success update over successful runs, with seeded percentile bootstrap interval
assumptions: Both stages condition on success by the same bound
P2.comparison: Supporting marginal comparison; fewer than two successes is INCONCLUSIVE

P3.description: Expected physical shots conditional on bounded success
P3.stage1: P2 times configured physical shots per update
P3.stage2: Successful-run resource consumption checked by N3 and compared with the conditional model mean
assumptions: Fixed candidate/group allocation with no hidden evaluations or retries
P3.comparison: Supporting statistical/resource comparison; scaled P2, not independent predictive evidence
